p.src: Now Wang Qing, seeing the bench behave strangely, kicked at it; but he used too much force, wrenched his ribs, and crouched on the ground crying, “What agony! What agony!” For a long while he could not move or straighten himself. His wife heard his cries and came out to look. Seeing the bench toppled to one side and her husband in such a state, she slapped Wang Qing across the face and said, “You useless monster! You spend every day away from home without a thought for the household. You only came home tonight, and already what have you been up to now?” Wang Qing said, “Wife, do not make fun of me. I have wrenched my ribs—it is unbearable!” The woman helped Wang Qing to his feet. Wang Qing hooked an arm over his wife’s shoulder and, shaking his head and gritting his teeth, cried, “Ah! It hurts terribly!” The woman cursed him: “You lecherous rogue, you damned crooked thing! You are forever delighting in kicking and punching, and today you have finally brought it out.” Realizing that her last words had an indecent double meaning, the woman covered her mouth with the sleeve of her gauze blouse and laughed. When Wang Qing heard the words “brought it out,” even in such pain he could not suppress his amusement and burst into loud laughter. The woman gave Wang Qing another slap and said, “You damned monster! What filthy thing are you imagining now?” The woman then helped Wang Qing onto the bed, cracked a plateful of walnut kernels, warmed a pot of wine, and gave them to him. She herself went to bar the doors, swat the mosquitoes, lower the bed curtains, and retire with her husband. Wang Qing’s waist and ribs hurt so badly that the particular member in question could not stir either—that goes without saying.

p.src: The night passed without further incident. Early the next morning Wang Qing’s pain had still not ceased. He wondered to himself how he could go before the officials, salute them, and answer their commands. He held out until noon, when his wife urged him to go out and buy some medicinal plasters. Wang Qing painfully shuffled to the prefectural offices. At a north-facing shop there, he bought two plasters from old Qian, who specialized in treating injuries from falls and blows, and applied them to his ribs. Old Qian said, “Captain, if you want to recover quickly, you must also take two doses of a decoction that heals injuries and quickens the blood.” With that, he measured out two doses of medicine and handed them to Wang Qing. Wang Qing took a piece of silver from his purse, weighing perhaps two or three candareens, asked for a sheet of paper, and wrapped the silver in it. The old man glanced sideways as he wrapped the silver, then pretended to turn his face eastward. Wang Qing held out the paper packet and said, “Sir, please do not despise this trifling gift. Use it to buy yourself a cooling melon.” Old Qian said, “Captain, why should friends reckon accounts so closely? I really cannot accept this!” Even as he continued protesting, however, his right hand had already accepted the packet; he lifted the lid of his medicine chest and dropped it inside.

p.src: Medicine in hand, Wang Qing was just about to rise when he saw a fortune-teller approaching along the street west of the prefectural offices. He wore a single-gauze kerchief tied low across his brow and a long robe of ramie cloth, and carried a parasol. From beneath it hung a paper sign bearing four large characters, “Divine Calculations of the Prior Heaven,” with sixteen smaller characters on either side: “Li Zhu of Jingnan—one calculation for ten cash; every word proves true; his art surpasses Guan Lu’s.”

p.src: Seeing that he was a fortune-teller, Wang Qing—who already had the matter of Jiaoxiu on his mind and had also encountered yesterday’s strange event—called out, “Master Li, please come and sit here.” The fortune-teller said, “What instruction does Your Honor have for me?” As he spoke, his eyes rolled keenly over Wang Qing from head to foot. Wang Qing said, “I should like to have my fortune told.” Li Zhu lowered his parasol and entered the plaster shop. Cupping his hands to old Qian, he said, “Pardon the intrusion!” From the sleeve of his unlined ramie robe he drew a red-sandalwood divining tube, opened its lid, took out a full-sized copper coin, and handed it to Wang Qing, saying, “Go over there and pray silently to Heaven.” Wang Qing took the divining coin, faced the blazing red sun, bent at the waist, and made his salute. But the pain kept him from bending properly. Like an old man of eighty or ninety, he held his back stiff, managed a half bow and half cupped-hand salute, then stood with face upturned and prayed. Watching from the shop, Li Zhu quietly ventured to old Qian, “With your plasters, sir, he is sure to recover quickly. I suppose he was injured in a fight?” Old Qian said, “He thought some bench was behaving strangely and wrenched his waist and ribs kicking it. When he first came just now, he was panting even as he spoke. After I put two plasters on him, he can bend his waist already.” Li Zhu said, “I thought he looked as though he had suffered a wrench.” When Wang Qing had finished praying, he handed the coin to Li Zhu. Li Zhu asked Wang Qing’s name, shook the divining tube, and chanted: “The day is auspicious, the hour propitious; Heaven and Earth unfold. The Sage fashioned the Changes, secretly aiding the divine intelligence. It encompasses the myriad forms, and its Way accords with Qian and Kun. Its virtue accords with Heaven and Earth, its brightness with sun and moon, its order with the four seasons, and its judgments of fortune and misfortune with ghosts and spirits. Now a gentleman surnamed Wang of the Kaifeng Prefecture in the Eastern Capital purchases a divination before Heaven. On the yimao day within the jiayin decade, we respectfully invite King Wen, first master of the Zhou Changes, the first master Guigu, and the first master Yuan Tiangang—supremely divine and sagely, supremely blessed and efficacious—to guide the perplexed and manifestly reveal retribution.”

p.src: Li Zhu cast from the divining tube twice and arranged the results into a hexagram. It was Zhun, Water over Thunder. After examining the movements of its six lines, he asked, “What matter is Your Honor consulting the oracle about?” Wang Qing said, “My household.” Shaking his head, Li Zhu said, “Your Honor must not blame me for speaking plainly. Zhun means difficulty: your calamities are only now beginning! I have several lines of judgment that Your Honor must remember.” Waving a folding oil-paper fan with bamboo ribs, Li Zhu recited: “The household falls into disorder; a hundred apparitions breed calamity, and the home knows no peace. If not an ancient temple, then a perilous bridge. The White Tiger brings a baleful clash; official trouble and sickness follow. What begins but has no end can never succeed; meeting the mighty brings frightful peril, lawsuits, and prison. The household is unsettled; there come falls and stumbles, while powerless limbs must be pried along with a crutch. Make a change, and quarrels will fade away. On days of Tiger, Dragon, Rooster, or Dog, baleful stars summon countless troubles and woes.”

p.src: Wang Qing sat facing Li Zhu, but could not endure the stink of persimmon varnish from the oil-paper fan, so he covered his nose with the sleeve of his black gauze robe as he listened. When Li Zhu had finished reciting, he said to Wang Qing, “I speak plainly according to the principles of the oracle: further strange happenings await in your home! You must reform your ways and move house; only then can you remain safe. Tomorrow is a bingchen day. You must be careful!” Hearing him predict such danger, Wang Qing no longer knew what to do. He took out some money and rewarded Li Zhu. Li Zhu left the medicine shop, raised his parasol, and went eastward. Just then five or six constables and runners from the prefectural offices saw Wang Qing and said, “Why are you idling here in conversation?” Wang Qing told them how he had seen the strange occurrence and wrenched himself, and they all laughed. Wang Qing said, “Gentlemen, if His Excellency the prefect asks about me, please smooth matters over for your brother here!” They all replied, “We understand what to do.” With that, they each went their separate ways.

p.src: Wang Qing returned home and told his wife to decoct the medicine. Eager to recover, Wang Qing swallowed both doses in less than four hours; and to make the medicine circulate, he drank several more cups of wine. He did not know that the medicines for treating injuries and invigorating the blood were all heating in nature. When he lay down that night, his wife pressed against him and fondled him, kindling his desire; but the pain in his waist kept him from moving. His wife, however, had long been left alone because Wang Qing had been carrying on with Jiaoxiu and staying away day and night. Her desire now blazed like fire; she would not let him escape, but climbed atop him and performed a “Rout of the Slender-Willow Camp.” The two slept straight through until the hour of the Dragon the next morning before rising. After washing and dressing, Wang Qing felt his stomach was empty and warmed some wine to drink. He was still eating breakfast when someone outside called, “Is the troop leader at home?” His wife peered through a crack in the plank wall and said, “They are two men from the prefecture.” At these words Wang Qing froze for a moment. He had no choice but to set down his rice bowl, wipe his mouth, and go outside. Cupping his hands, he asked, “What instruction brings you gentlemen here?” The two constables said, “The troop leader certainly knows how to enjoy himself! Such a fine flush on your face this early in the morning! His Honor called the roll this morning, and when you failed to appear, he flew into a rage. We fellows reported on your behalf that you had hurt your back after seeing that apparition, but would he believe us? He issued a summons at once and sent the two of us to bring you in for an explanation.” They showed the summons to Wang Qing. Wang Qing said, “My face is flushed now. How can I present myself before him? It would be better to wait a little while.” The two constables said, “That is no concern of ours. His Honor is waiting for your answer this very moment. If we are late, you will only get us beaten as well. Come quickly! Come quickly!” The two supported Wang Qing between them and set off. Wang Qing’s wife hurried out to ask what was happening, but her husband had already gone through the door.

p.src: The two constables supported Wang Qing into the Kaifeng Prefecture, where the prefect sat in the hall upon a tiger-skin chair. They brought Wang Qing forward and reported, “In obedience to Your Honor’s command, we have brought Wang Qing.” With great difficulty, Wang Qing knocked his head four times toward the bench. The prefect shouted, “Wang Qing, you are a soldier. How dare you neglect your duty and fail to attend?” Wang Qing once more recounted in detail how he had seen the apparition and hurt his back, saying, “The pain in my waist and ribs is real. I can neither sit nor lie in peace, and I am unable to walk. I would never dare neglect my duty. I beg Your Excellency to show me indulgence.” When the prefect had heard him out and saw that Wang Qing’s face was flushed, he flew into a rage and shouted, “You scoundrel! You do nothing but get drunk, commit outrages, and break the law. Today you have even fabricated this monstrous tale to deceive your superior!” He ordered the guards to drag him away and beat him. How could Wang Qing possibly make himself understood? They beat Wang Qing until his skin split and his flesh burst, forcing him to confess to fabricating a seditious book, inciting the ignorant populace, and plotting rebellion. Wang Qing had been wrung dry by his wife the night before and was tortured by the authorities today—truly two axes felling one tree. He fainted and revived, and at last, unable to endure the beating, made a false confession. The prefect recorded Wang Qing’s deposition, then ordered the jailers to bring a cangue and shackles, fasten them upon him, and commit him to death row, intending to prosecute him for the capital crime of fabricating a seditious book and plotting rebellion. The jailers carried Wang Qing, battered and bleeding, into the prison.

p.src: It turned out that Tong Guan had secretly sent someone to instruct the prefect to find a charge on which to dispose of Wang Qing, and this strange affair had arisen at precisely the right moment. By then everyone high and low in the prefecture knew of Wang Qing’s affair with Jiaoxiu, and the rumor spread everywhere: “Wang Qing has been condemned because of that business. This time he certainly will not survive.” When this reached the ears of Cai Jing and Cai You, father and son found it most unpleasant. They discussed the matter and concluded that if Wang Qing were put to death, the story would seem all the more credible and the scandal would spread even farther. They therefore secretly enlisted a trusted official who was on intimate terms with the prefect, instructing him to have Wang Qing tattooed and exiled without delay to some distant and inhospitable military prefecture, thereby erasing all trace of the affair. Cai Jing and Cai You selected an auspicious day for Cai You’s son to marry Jiaoxiu: first to conceal Tong Guan’s disgrace, and second to silence public gossip. Cai You’s son was a fool in any event and could not tell whether Jiaoxiu was a virgin or not; but that is beside the point.

p.src: Now the prefect of Kaifeng, acting on the confidential message from Grand Preceptor Cai’s trusted agent, immediately ascended the bench. That day was a xinyou day. Wang Qing was brought out of prison, relieved of his long cangue, and sentenced to twenty strokes across the back. A tattooer was summoned to brand his cheeks; then, the distance of his destination having been calculated, he was assigned to the prison fortress of Shanzhou under the Western Capital. There in the hall they fastened upon him a round-headed, iron-plated protective cangue weighing ten and a half catties, affixed the official seal, and issued an escort warrant. Two convoy constables, Sun Lin and He Ji, were assigned to guard him on the journey.

p.src: When the three emerged from the Kaifeng Prefecture, they found Wang Qing’s father-in-law, Squire Niu, waiting for them. He accompanied Wang Qing, Sun Lin, and He Ji to a tavern on South Street before the yamen, where they sat down. Squire Niu ordered the waiter to bring wine and meat. After they had drunk several cups, he took a packet of small silver pieces from his person, held it out to Wang Qing, and said, “Here are thirty taels of silver for your expenses on the road.” Wang Qing reached for it, saying, “Many thanks, Father-in-law!” Squire Niu pushed Wang Qing’s hand away and said, “Not so fast! I would not ordinarily give you money for nothing. Now you are being exiled to Shanzhou, more than a thousand li away across distant roads and mountains. Who knows when you will return? You dallied with another man’s daughter, yet it is your own wife you have left in the lurch! Who is to support your wife? You have neither son nor daughter to keep your fields and property until you return. You must write a bill of divorce allowing her to remarry freely after your departure, so there will be no dispute in days to come. Only then will I give you the silver.” Wang Qing was ordinarily a spendthrift. He thought, “I have not even ten taels or half a catty of silver in my purse. How could I ever reach Shaanxi?” He turned it over again and again in his mind, and needing the silver for expenses, sighed twice and said, “So be it! So be it! I have no choice but to write the bill of divorce.” Squire Niu took the document with one hand and handed over the silver with the other, then returned home.

p.src: Wang Qing returned home with the two constables to pack his baggage, only to find that his wife had already been taken back to Squire Niu’s house and the door was locked. Wang Qing borrowed an axe and chisel from a neighbor and broke open the door. When he went inside, he found that everything his wife had worn on her body or put in her hair had been taken away. Wang Qing was both enraged and heartbroken. He asked an old woman named Zhou who lived next door to prepare some wine and food at his house for the constables. Then he presented Sun Lin and He Ji with ten taels of silver, saying, “The wounds from my beating are painful, and I cannot walk. I would like to rest for several days before setting out.” Sun Lin and He Ji accepted the money and agreed, but unfortunately Cai You had enlisted a trusted agent to press the constables to depart. Wang Qing hastily sold off his household goods and surrendered the rented house to Squire Hu’s family.

u.src: Wang Qing returned home with the two constables to pack his baggage, only to find that his wife had already been taken back to Squire Niu’s house and the door was locked.
Wang Qing borrowed an axe and chisel from a neighbor and broke open the door. When he went inside, he found that everything his wife had worn on her body or put in her hair had been taken away.
Wang Qing was both enraged and heartbroken.

He asked an old woman named Zhou who lived next door to prepare some wine and food at his house for the constables. Then he presented Sun Lin and He Ji with ten taels of silver, saying, “The wounds from my beating are painful, and I cannot walk. I would like to rest for several days before setting out.”
Sun Lin and He Ji accepted the money and agreed, but unfortunately Cai You had enlisted a trusted agent to press the constables to depart.
Wang Qing hastily sold off his household goods and surrendered the rented house to Squire Hu’s family.

p.src: By this time, Wang Qing's father, Wang Xue, had been so angered by his son that he had gone blind in both eyes. He lived apart, and whenever his son came to his door, he would either strike or curse him. But today, when he heard that his son had fallen foul of the law and been sentenced to penal exile, his heart ached despite himself. He had a young servant support him to Wang Qing's room and called out, “Oh, my son! You would not heed my admonitions, and now it has come to this.” When he had finished speaking, tears fell from those dim, sightless eyes. From childhood, Wang Qing had never once called Wang Xue “Father.” Yet now, with his family ruined and its members scattered, sorrow welled up in him too, and he cried, “Father, your son has suffered a terrible injustice today. That wretched old Niu was so outrageous that he forced me to write a letter divorcing my wife before he would give me the silver.” Wang Xue said, “You have always loved your wife and honored your father-in-law. How is it that he treats you this way today?” Stung by these two reproachful remarks, Wang Qing angrily ignored his father and went straight off with the two constables, gathering his things and leaving the city. Wang Xue stamped his feet and beat his breast, crying, “I should never have come to see that ungrateful wretch!” Then, supported once more by the young servant, he returned home. Of him we shall say no more.

p.src: Now Wang Qing, together with Sun Lin and He Ji, left the Eastern Capital. They rented lodging in a secluded place, where he recuperated for more than ten days. Once the wounds from his beating had somewhat healed, the constables urged him onward, and they traveled gradually toward Shanzhou. It was then early in the sixth month, and the weather was sweltering. They could travel only forty or fifty li a day, and on the road they inevitably slept in beds vacated by the dead and ate food with scarcely a warm sip of broth. The three traveled for fifteen or sixteen days and passed Mount Song. One day, as they were walking, Sun Lin pointed toward the distant peaks in the west and said, “That mountain is called Mount Beimang. It lies under the jurisdiction of the Western Capital.” Talking as they went, the three took advantage of the cool morning air and covered more than twenty li. East of Mount Beimang they saw a market town, toward which farmers from all the surrounding villages were streaming. At the sparsely inhabited eastern end of the town stood three great cypresses arranged like the strokes of the character ding. Deep shade lay beneath the trees. There, a dense crowd stood shoulder to shoulder around a bare-chested man who was shouting and flourishing a staff in the cool shade. The three went beneath the trees to rest in the shade. Wang Qing was drenched in sweat from walking, his whole body hot and clammy. Still wearing the protective cangue, he squeezed into the crowd and stood on tiptoe to watch the man wield his staff. After watching for a while, Wang Qing inadvertently laughed aloud and said, “That fellow is only flourishing a showman's staff.” The man was just reaching the most exciting part of his display. Hearing this remark, he lowered his staff and looked, only to see a convict in exile. The man flew into a rage and cursed him: “You thieving convict! My spear and staff arts are renowned far and wide, yet you dare open that filthy beak of yours, belittle my skill, and let out such a fart!” He threw down his staff, raised his fists, and struck straight at Wang Qing's face. At once two young men stepped out of the crowd and stopped him, saying, “Do not resort to blows!” Then they asked Wang Qing, “You, sir, must surely be a master.” Wang Qing replied, “I spoke one careless word and provoked that man's anger. I have only a slight acquaintance with the arts of spear and staff.” The staff-wielding man over there cursed furiously, “You thieving convict! Do you dare have a match with me?” The two young men said to Wang Qing, “Will you cross staves with that fellow? If you defeat him, we shall give you the full two strings of cash collected here.” Wang Qing laughed. “Very well.” He parted the crowd, took a staff from He Ji, stripped off his sweat-soaked shirt, tucked up his robe, and drew the staff into his hands. Everyone said, “You have a cangue around your neck. How can you possibly swing a staff?” Wang Qing said, “That is precisely what makes it remarkable. Only if I defeat him while wearing this traveling cangue will it count as true skill.” The crowd cried in unison, “If you defeat him while wearing the cangue, those two strings of cash will certainly be yours!” They cleared a path and let Wang Qing enter the ring. The staff-wielding man also drew his weapon into his hands, assumed a formal opening posture, and shouted, “Come on! Come on! Come on!” Wang Qing said, “Good sirs, please do not laugh at me.” The other man plainly counted on Wang Qing being hindered by his protective cangue. He opened with a stance called “The Python Swallows the Elephant.” Wang Qing likewise assumed a stance, called “The Dragonfly Skims the Water.” With a shout, the man brought his staff crashing down upon him. Wang Qing stepped back. The man pursued him by one stride, raised his staff, and again brought it down toward the crown of Wang Qing's head. Wang Qing dodged to the left. The man's staff struck empty air, and he could not recover it in time. In the very motion of that dodge, Wang Qing chopped his staff toward the man's right hand. It struck him squarely on the wrist and knocked the staff from his grasp. Fortunately, Wang Qing had held back his force; otherwise, he would have broken the man's wrist. The crowd burst into laughter. Wang Qing stepped forward, took the man's hand, and said, “Forgive my offense!” The man's right hand was in pain, so he reached with his left for the two strings of cash.

p.src: The two men invited Wang Qing and the two constables along. All five put on coolie hats, headed south through two or three groves, and came to a village. Within the grove stood a large manor, surrounded on every side by earthen walls, outside which grew two or three hundred great willow trees. Outside the manor, new cicadas clamored in the willows; within, fledgling swallows chirped beneath the beams. The two men led Wang Qing and his companions into the manor and on to the thatched hall. When the courtesies were over, everyone took off his sweat-soaked shirt and hempen shoes, and host and guests seated themselves in their proper places. The master of the manor asked, “You gentlemen all sound as though you come from the Eastern Capital.” Wang Qing gave his name and related how the prefect had framed him. When he had finished, he asked the two men for their honored names. The two were delighted. The man in the upper seat said, “My humble surname is Gong, and my given name is Duan. This is my younger brother, whose given name is Zheng. Our family has lived here for generations, and that is why this place is called Gong Family Village. It lies under the jurisdiction of Xin’an County in the Western Capital.” After speaking, he ordered the farmhands to wash the three guests’ drenched shirts. First he had cool water drawn to quench their heat and thirst, then led them to the main rooms for baths. A table was set in the thatched hall, where they first ate some ready-made refreshments; afterward chickens and ducks were slaughtered, beans cooked and peaches picked, and wine laid on for their entertainment. The farmhands set the table afresh. First they brought out a dish of peeled garlic and another of thick scallions cut into lengths, followed by vegetables, fruit, fish, meat, chicken, duck, and other foods. Gong Duan invited Wang Qing to take the upper seat, with the two constables seated beside him. Gong Duan and his brother laid places for themselves below, and a farmhand poured the wine. Wang Qing thanked them, saying, “I am a convicted prisoner. It is more kindness than I deserve for you both to favor me so, and it is quite improper that I should intrude upon you without cause.” Gong Duan replied, “What are you saying! Who can guarantee that trouble will never befall him? Who travels through life carrying his own food and wine?” They drank and played drinking games, and when the wine had brought them to half-drunkenness, Gong Duan began: “There are more than two hundred households in this humble village and its surroundings, and they all look to my brother and me as their leaders. My brother and I also know something of fists and staves, enough to keep the people in submission. In the second month of this spring, the eastern village held a festival for the gods and raised a stage for theatrical performances. My brother and I went over to enjoy ourselves, but quarreled over gambling with a man of that village named Huang Da. The brute gave us a sound beating, and even together we could not defeat him. That scoundrel Huang Da boasted of his prowess before everyone. Since the two of us could do nothing against him, we had no choice but to swallow our anger and endure the humiliation. Just now we saw how precise and well-ordered your staff technique was, Instructor. We wish to acknowledge you as our master and beg you to give us brothers some guidance. We shall certainly reward you handsomely.” Wang Qing was delighted to hear this, though he modestly declined for a time. Gong Duan and his brother then at once acknowledged Wang Qing as their master. That evening they drank until they were thoroughly drunk, and only then stopped to rest in the cool air.

p.src: At daybreak the next morning, Wang Qing took advantage of the early coolness to instruct Gong Duan in punches and kicks on the threshing ground. Suddenly a man appeared outside, strolling in with his hands clasped behind his back. He shouted, “What banished convict dares come here to show off his skills?” Because this man walked in, Wang Qing was destined to sow the seeds of another great calamity, while Gong Duan would incur yet another bitter enmity. Truly, disaster springs from reckless conduct, and disgrace is summoned by gambling. But who was this man who had entered Gong Duan’s manor? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
